title: What are you doing this week?
content_html:
Interesting, from the video, "the temporal contract" is what I'm building next.

I started with Obsidian after using Logseq briefly, developing a multi-tenant LiveSync clone in Go, but even 1 second was too long for me to wait to get it to sync (I aim for <200ms load times and get a little frustrated if anything in the 21st century takes considerably longer than 100ms). I did really enjoy LogSeq and Obsidian, but developing some basic MCP tools and seeing how it organised the stuff I vomited into it made me realise it's better at organising than I will ever be, I like where it puts stuff, and treated it more like an ebook reader, sometimes I was reading my own notes for the first time.

Now, I've found the best results using a web page with a single text field, just an idea.

(After Claude and Codex did their best to cater for users who did not know about shift+ins and middle click and messed up terminal formatting, linebreaks, etc, I gave up with trying to insert newlines and instead separated everything with --/- consistently, so I am biased with regards to articulating myself in one long unbroken wall of text, as you can see)

I wanted to do something fundamentally different, where data can be multiple kinds all at once. You have an idea when journalling, or schedule an appointment. The diary entry is the base truth, but it can spark an idea. Does my journalling then irreversibly turn into ideation? No, and that's the key for me. You just write, but what you write can have effects in the future based on what that is, and if you want to see why, you can read exactly what you were thinking when you made that commitment, what state of mind you were in, what your resting heart rate was, HRV, how long you slept, any impulsive purchases you made, etc (all real examples currently possible, I'm not spitballing, I ran out of ideas because I implemented most of them now I'm going meta -.-)

I've long considered how I might integrate Obsidian into the idea system, and how editing the note would cause database object skew, or how, if backed directly by Obsidian, deleting notes/lines would cause related objects to break. It's quite involved -- It's currently based on PostgreSQL and uses a CouchDB translation layer, so I can use Postgres and clients can speak CouchDB, allowing them to use the official integration. Needless to say, such a system is a massive pain in the ass, but it seems to actually work.

Here's a series of screenshots showing how the cycles work: https://blog.zm.is/when-do-your-good-ideas-happen/

Tomorrow I start work on the 21 ideas I already have listed after combining related ones into plans. However, one of those is to implement automated idea allocation

Tomorrow I start work on the 22 ideas I already have listed, hopefully I can start submitting therapy notes by the evening in my diary.

content_html_zh:
有趣的是，从视频来看，“时间契约”是我接下来要构建的。

在短暂使用 Logseq 后，我开始使用 Obsidian，在 Go 中开发了一个多租户 LiveSync 克隆，但即使 1 秒对我来说也太长了，无法等待它同步（我的目标是 <200 毫秒加载时间，如果 21 世纪的任何东西需要比 100 毫秒长得多的时间，我会有点沮丧）。 我确实很喜欢 LogSeq 和 Obsidian，但是开发了一些基本的 MCP 工具并看到它如何组织我吐出来的东西，让我意识到它比我以往任何时候都更擅长组织，我喜欢它放置东西的位置，并且更像是一个电子书阅读器，有时我是第一次阅读自己的笔记。

现在，我已经找到了使用带有单个文本字段的网页的最佳结果，这只是一个想法。

（在 Claude 和 Codex 尽最大努力迎合那些不了解 shift+ins 和中键单击以及弄乱终端格式、换行符等的用户之后，我放弃了尝试插入换行符，而是用 --/- 一致地分隔所有内容，所以我对在长长的不间断文本墙中阐明自己有偏见，如您所见）

我想做一些根本不同的事情，其中​​数据可以同时有多种类型。 当你写日记或安排约会时，你有一个想法。 日记内容是基本事实，但它可以激发一个想法。 我的日记会不可逆转地变成想法吗？ 不，这对我来说是关键。 你只是写，但你写的东西可能会根据它的内容在未来产生影响，如果你想知道为什么，你可以准确地读到你做出承诺时的想法，你的心态是什么，你的静息心率是多少，HRV，你睡了多长时间，你做出的任何冲动购买等等（目前所有真实的例子都是可能的，我不是在吐痰，我已经没有想法了，因为我实现了其中的大部分，现在我要去元-.-）

我长期以来一直在考虑如何将 Obsidian 集成到创意系统中，以及编辑注释将如何导致数据库对象倾斜，或者如果由 Obsidian 直接支持，删除注释/行将如何导致相关对象损坏。 它非常复杂——它目前基于 PostgreSQL 并使用 CouchDB 翻译层，因此我可以使用 Postgres，并且客户端可以使用 CouchDB，从而允许他们使用官方集成。 不用说，这样的系统是一个巨大的痛苦，但它似乎确实有效。

以下是一系列屏幕截图，显示了周期的工作原理：https://blog.zm.is/when-do-your-good-ideas-happen/

明天我将开始研究我已经列出的 21 个想法，并将相关想法合并到计划中。 然而，其中之一是实现自动化创意分配

明天我开始研究我已经列出的 22 个想法，希望我能在晚上之前开始在日记中提交治疗笔记。
